title: Mitchell, Phillips stand resolute to force a stalemate in Wellington
excerpt: Only three wickets fell on a lifeless Basin Reserve surface on Day 5, as Mitchell and Phillips played out 43 overs together rather comfortably
author: Cricbuzz Staff
body: New Zealand produced a determined batting effort to deny India a victory in the first Test in Wellington, grinding out 120 overs in their second innings to secure a draw. Despite losing two wickets in the morning session on the final day, the hosts frustrated India through the day, with Daryl Mitchell (49* off 186) and Glenn Phillips (26* off 126) adding an unbroken 63-run stand to take their side to 239 for 5.

It was a slow and windy morning in Wellington, with only 38 runs coming off the 26 overs bowled in the first session at a rate of 1.46. India, however, managed to break through twice, ending a stubborn second-wicket partnership between Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra that had yielded 72 runs in more than 200 deliveries. The pair had largely been content to see off the Indian bowlers with their defensive approach, and the occasional boundary. Nearly an hour into the session, Washington Sundar finally broke through, aided by the wind that helped generate some drift. Conway (65 off 165) got an inside edge that deflected off his pad and ballooned into Rishabh Pant's gloves. Meanwhile, Jasprit Bumrah was handed an official warning for running on the pitch.

Shubman Gill rotated his bowling options, bringing Prasidh Krishna into the attack in the second hour. The lanky pacer struck when Ravindra went for a drive but was undone by a ball that stopped a bit on him, resulting in an edge to gully where KL Rahul took a sharp catch. Ravindra departed for 37 off 129. Tom Blundell and Daryl Mitchell then dug in, negotiating the remainder of the session without further damage.

Early in the second session, India missed a run-out opportunity to give Mitchell a lucky break as Akash Deep did not gather the ball properly at mid on. Skipper Gill was livid with the effort but a couple of overs later, he managed a smile as Anshul Kamboj got Blundell to edge behind, with India using the DRS to get the decision in their favour, leaving New Zealand at 176 for 5. India took the second new ball at the start of the 83rd over, with Bumrah getting the first crack, and Akash Deep from the other end. Mitchell and Glenn Phillips managed a boundary each ahead of the drinks break.

Phillips punched Akash Deep through cover for a four to take New Zealand past 200. Prasidh replaced Bumrah and had Mitchell in trouble, but the absence of a fielder at forward short-leg, for what would have been a simple catch, denied India another chance. The umpire's call of not-out saved Phillips when Washington rapped him on the pad and India opted for the DRS. Mitchell and Phillips saw through the period before Tea, with New Zealand keeping India at bay in another slow session that yielded 49 runs in 25 overs, at a scoring rate of 1.96, for one wicket.

Washington went for runs at the start of the third session as Mitchell targeted him and started scoring freely, including a pull for the first six of the innings. Kamboj didn't create any chances from the other end either, as Mitchell and Blundell raised a half-century stand. Akash Deep came on soon enough and bowled stump to stump lines with the 'keeper up, with Washington continuing from the other end. But they weren't able to make inroads despite keeping things tight, with Gill eventually turning to Bumrah again.

Bumrah tried his best to break through, as did Prasidh who came on sometime later, but to no avail as Mitchell and Phillips remained untroubled on a Day 5 pitch that still wasn't offering anything even into the final session. They burned a review when Washington pinned Mitchell on the pad, with the ball having pitched outside leg. Even Yashasvi Jaiswal and Dhruv Jurel were given the ball but the New Zealand batters didn't budge as Mitchell and Phillips saw off 258 deliveries in the sixth wicket partnership, before the players shook hands ahead of the final hour.

Barring the five-wicket burst on Day 1, it was hard work for the bowlers throughout the Test match. New Zealand posted 368 in the first innings after being reduced to 70 for 5, with Henry Nicholls (175*) and Phillips (118) coming to the home team's rescue. India responded with 720 for 9 declared, riding on six fifty-plus scores - centuries for Rahul and Pant, 98 for Gill, 80s from Jaiswal and Devdutt Padikkal, and 78 by Jurel. New Zealand's second-innings effort was led by Conway (65) and Mitchell, ensuring that the contest ended in a stalemate.

Brief scores: New Zealand 368 (Henry Nicholls 175*, Glenn Phillips 118; Jasprit Bumrah 4-92, Akash Deep 3-53) & 239/5 (Devon Conway 65, Daryl Mitchell 49*; Prasidh Krishna 2-23) drew with India 720/9 decl. (KL Rahul 136, Rishabh Pant 128, Shubman Gill 98, Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, Devdutt Padikkal 80, Dhruv Jurel 78; Glenn Phillips 3-154).
